observations.behavior: Replaces the previous document identity strategy. Instead of creating a new KnowledgeSource and deriving a document ID from it, the code now computes a stable ID from the ticket and resolution context, then looks up or creates a KnowledgeSource using that stable ID. This changes the document identity and deduplication behavior.
observations.posthog_connection: This could change how PostHog stores and retrieves generated business knowledge. If the stable ID computation or the lookup of the KnowledgeSource fails, the document may not be created or may be assigned an unexpected ID, potentially breaking downstream retrieval or deduplication.

observations.behavior: Adds a check against a team-wide learned-source quota before creating a KnowledgeSource. If the team has reached the maximum, it raises LearnedSourceCapReached.
observations.posthog_connection: This could prevent a team from creating more than a configured number of learned sources. If the quota is reached, the learning workflow is rejected rather than failing later, potentially avoiding resource exhaustion or unexpected behavior.

observations.behavior: Updates the comment and implementation to distinguish between user-managed and generated sources. Generated sources update the existing document in place rather than deleting and recreating, while user-managed sources delete and recreate.
observations.posthog_connection: This could preserve document identity for generated sources during edits, while user-managed sources retain their delete-and-recreate behavior. This could affect downstream workflows that depend on document identity stability.
